inspection_summary: Inspected all 921 normalized lines. The source builds a phase-based representation of intersections of the critical-line zeta curve with arbitrary lines through the origin, counts the phase roots by winding, evaluates first and second discrete moments by a residue-contour/functional-equation method, derives directional large-value and nonzero-crossing consequences, translates the results to Gram points, and records both a geometric heuristic and a higher-degree L-function obstruction. The prose is coherent; displayed formulas have text-layer spacing damage but remain recoverable from their checked local prose.

accepted_units.title: Phase roots encode intersections with any line through the origin
accepted_units.why_material: The functional equation and unit-modulus phase factor turn the geometric condition that zeta lies on eiφR into a root condition for Φ, while separating zeta zeros from roots of a rotating phase equation; this is the paper's reusable bridge from planar value distribution to discrete sampling.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the definitions of Δ, Φ, the argument condition, and the decomposition of the intersection count; the exponent notation at line 99 is text-layer damaged but its role is fixed by lines 66-86.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on complex conjugation, the functional equation, and the unit-circle representation of Δ; retain displayed equations (1)-(2) and verify exponent glyphs against the scan before formula-level reuse.

accepted_units.title: Counting and moment laws for directional critical-line intersections
accepted_units.why_material: Gives the phase-root counting asymptotic and the first two discrete moments of zeta over intersections with eiφR, including the structural contrast that the leading second moment is direction-independent while the first varies as eiφ cos φ.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 span. It is coherent as a theorem block, but its symbols and the distinction between all intersections and phase roots require the setup at lines 56-100 for standalone v2 use.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on exact displayed asymptotics (Theorems 1-2), phase parameter φ, and the counting functions introduced earlier; formula layout should be scan-checked before transcription.

accepted_units.title: Directional means and arbitrarily large values on half-lines
accepted_units.why_material: Translates the counting and moment laws into conditional directional means, an unconditional zero mean on the imaginary axis, positivity of real components, and unconditional arbitrarily large values on prescribed right-half-plane half-lines.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 span. The proof dependencies are the counting and two moment statements at lines 117-170, and the conditional normalization changes with RH versus the unconditional imaginary-axis case.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on complex-line orientation, the difference between a line and a half-line, and the displayed mean/large-value inequalities; preserve the RH qualifications exactly.

accepted_units.title: Nonzero phase crossings and the missing imaginary-axis bound
accepted_units.why_material: Separates phase roots that coincide with zeta zeros from genuine nonzero intersections, gives a directional lower bound away from φ=π/2, and identifies Fujii's proposed equidistribution of zero phases as a route to information in the exceptional direction.
accepted_units.context_note: The figure at lines 245-248 is illustrative context; the semantic core is Corollary 5 and the explicit statement of why the purely imaginary case remains unresolved.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the exact exclusion ζ(1/2+it)≠0 and on a formula whose extracted exponent spacing is fragile; scan verification is needed for the numerical lower-bound constant.

accepted_units.title: Monotone phase rotation converts root counts to a winding number
accepted_units.why_material: Uses the logarithmic derivative asymptotic to show that Δ rotates monotonically with increasing speed, identifies roots of a prescribed phase with a winding number, integrates the rotation rate, and removes a convenient endpoint assumption with a controlled error.
accepted_units.context_note: The temporary endpoint condition Δ(1/2+iT)=1 is only a proof device and is explicitly removed at lines 323-325.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the orientation/sign of the winding integral and the asymptotic for Δ'/Δ; displayed integral typography should be scan-checked for exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: Residues sample zeta at phase roots under a separated endpoint choice
accepted_units.why_material: Introduces a variation of the Conrey-Ghosh-Gonek method in which the logarithmic derivative of Δ-e^{2iφ} provides poles at the desired sampling ordinates, chooses an endpoint separated from them, and expresses the first discrete moment as four contour contributions.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the bounded treatment of low/off-line roots and the T-dependent narrow rectangle; later units determine which contour sides contribute main terms.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the rectangle geometry, residue multiplicities, and the denominator Δ(s)-e^{2iφ}; preserve contour orientation and the endpoint separation bound.

accepted_units.title: Suppress three contour sides and reflect the main side
accepted_units.why_material: Uses rapid geometric-series expansions and growth bounds to make the right, top, and bottom sides negligible, then reflects the left side through s↦1-s and the functional equation so its integrand becomes a tractable Dirichlet-series kernel.
accepted_units.context_note: Ends at the decomposition I3=J1+J2+error; the subsequent evaluation is kept in a separate unit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on half-plane size comparisons for Δ, the critical-line separation estimate, conjugation/reflection, and geometric-series convergence.

accepted_units.title: Gonek's lemma isolates the two components of the first moment
accepted_units.why_material: Evaluates the reflected contour's two principal pieces: Gonek's lemma extracts the diagonal-scale term from ζ(s)Δ(1-s), while direct integration of ζ(s) supplies the phase-weighted companion; their combination yields 1+e^{2iφ}=2e^{iφ}cosφ.
accepted_units.context_note: The extension from separated endpoints to arbitrary T is included and uses a pointwise zeta bound to absorb the final sample.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the exact transform kernel in Lemma 6, the phase factor, and partial integration; formula glyphs are recoverable but should be scan-verified before executable use.

accepted_units.title: The first-moment contour architecture lifts to the square
accepted_units.why_material: Shows how the same phase-root residue kernel is reused for ζ(s)ζ(1-s), with one contour side now contributing a phase-dependent lower-order term and the reflected side producing ζ(s)^2Δ'(1-s).
accepted_units.context_note: This span records the changed integrand and decomposition rather than repeating all earlier side estimates, making the method comparison explicit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the functional equation converting ζ(s)ζ(1-s), the same contour and geometric-series regime, and exact phase exponents.

accepted_units.title: A divisor-sum diagonal produces the second moment's leading square logarithm
accepted_units.why_material: Applies Gonek's lemma to ζ(s)^2Δ(1-s), converts the result to a divisor summatory asymptotic, and combines it with the phase-dependent companion term to obtain the second-moment expansion.
accepted_units.context_note: The leading term is independent of direction; φ enters at lower order through the second principal piece.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the Dirichlet divisor estimate, Euler's constant, and displayed logarithmic coefficients; scan verification is needed before coefficient-level reuse.

accepted_units.title: Conditional and unconditional denominators yield different mean-value conclusions
accepted_units.why_material: Makes explicit that the same first-moment numerator becomes a full directional mean under RH through Nφ(T) asymptotics, while the imaginary-axis zero mean follows unconditionally because its main term vanishes and the phase-root count supplies a sufficient denominator.
accepted_units.context_note: Also records how the known positive proportion of critical-line zeros yields only liminf/limsup bounds in general.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on distinguishing Nφ from NφΔ and on preserving the RH and φ=π/2 branches.

accepted_units.title: Second-moment mass forces a large value in every dyadic interval
accepted_units.why_material: Compares the number of phase samples in (T,2T] with their second-moment mass to rule out a uniform sub-square-root-log bound, then uses the signed first moment to force the desired half-line sign; the exceptional imaginary direction uses its zero-mean relation to obtain both signs.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the proof mechanism behind the large-value statement already carried in u02.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on dyadic restriction, moment exponents, and oriented values e^{-iφ}ζ; the sign conclusion is not supplied by the second moment alone.

accepted_units.title: Cauchy-Schwarz turns moments into a count of nonzero phase crossings
accepted_units.why_material: Relates the squared first moment to the product of the nonzero-sample count and second moment, yielding the lower bound for genuine line crossings after inserting the two moment asymptotics.
accepted_units.context_note: Short but reusable bridge: it explains both the origin and the directional degeneration of Corollary 5.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on excluding zero zeta values in the counting factor and on the exact first-moment directional coefficient.

accepted_units.title: Gram points recast real-axis intersections and expose failures of sign alternation
accepted_units.why_material: Specializes the phase roots to Gram points, introduces the real Hardy Z-function, relates sign changes to critical-line zeros, and interprets failures of Gram's law as negative real-axis intersections whose unbounded magnitude remains open.
accepted_units.context_note: Historical claims serve the mathematical obstruction: matching counts do not guarantee persistent interlacing or sign alternation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the phase convention for θ and the sign normalization (-1)^nZ(tn); retain those conventions when comparing formulations.

accepted_units.title: Directional moments imply lower growth of fourth moments at Gram points
accepted_units.why_material: Translates the paper's first and second moment asymptotics into sums over Gram points and combines the second moment with Cauchy-Schwarz to force a fourth-moment lower bound, complementing prior upper-bound work.
accepted_units.context_note: The earlier neighboring-product results motivate the question but are distinct from the derived single-point fourth-moment lower bound.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the asymptotic relation between Gram index and ordinate and on the Hardy Z normalization.

accepted_units.title: Averaging directional means suggests a small-versus-large intersection split
accepted_units.why_material: Integrates the conditional means e^{iφ}cosφ over direction to obtain 1/2, relates that value to a separate a-point derivative phenomenon, and proposes the heuristic that each directional intersection set divides roughly equally between very small and large magnitudes around its mean.
accepted_units.context_note: The final small/large split is explicitly heuristic; the mean statements retain their RH qualification where stated.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on viewing directions modulo π, the identity 2e^{iφ}cosφ=1+e^{2iφ}, and the comparison with the stated a-point asymptotic.

accepted_units.title: The method extends to Dirichlet L-functions but encounters higher-degree factorization barriers
accepted_units.why_material: Records that the mechanism transfers easily to Dirichlet L-functions but becomes difficult for higher-degree L-functions, with quadratic Dedekind zeta treated only by exploiting the factorization ζK=ζL and zero symmetry.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a scope/obstruction statement rather than a proved universal impossibility.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the availability of a suitable factorization and compatible functional-equation symmetry.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Phase discretization as a bridge from curve geometry to analytic sampling
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A unit-modulus functional-equation factor can discretize intersections of an analytic value curve with a chosen direction, after which winding counts and logarithmic-derivative residues provide matched cardinality and sampled-value statistics.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Established here only for the stated zeta/Δ setting; shared phase structure and suitable analytic control must be rechecked for any transfer.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Moments become geometric information only after the correct count and sign controls
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The sample count normalizes a first moment into a directional mean, the second moment forces large samples, and the signed first moment or a zero-mean symmetry is separately needed to place those samples on a desired half-line.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: General directional normalization is conditional on RH or almost-all critical-line zeros, while the imaginary-axis branch has a distinct unconditional argument.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Gram-law failure and Gram-point moments are two views of real-axis phase sampling
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Specializing the phase to the real axis makes negative intersections equivalent to failures of the normalized Gram sign rule, while the same discrete moments impose aggregate growth constraints on Hardy Z values at Gram points.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source does not determine whether negative real intersections have unbounded magnitude, and aggregate moments do not restore pointwise Gram interlacing.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The contour method's portability is governed by structural factorization
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The proof depends not merely on a functional equation but on phase-factor expansions and Dirichlet-series kernels whose main terms remain tractable; factorization supplies that tractability in the cited quadratic Dedekind case.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The paper states difficulty for higher degree and one successful factored case, not a necessary-and-sufficient transfer criterion.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Directional means form a coherent planar picture but not a density theorem
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The family e^{iφ}cosφ traces a circle of conditional directional means and averages to 1/2, offering a geometric account of the positive-real tendency and a heuristic small/large split.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Neither the mean circle nor the heuristic split proves density of critical-line zeta values in the complex plane.
